speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent, and I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin my assessment, how long has the breathing difficulty been present, and was your delivery term or premature?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your prematurity at 33 weeks and the onset of distress just two hours after birth, I need to know if you are experiencing grunting, nasal flaring, or retractions, and whether you required any resuscitation immediately after delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The clinical picture of a 33-week premature infant presenting with respiratory distress, grunting, retractions, and cyanosis within two hours of birth is highly characteristic of surfactant deficiency.
